items.summary: The book series The Stream and the Algebra presents a speculative research programme — a thought-experiment in the mathematics of relation, offered for scrutiny, not yet peer-reviewed or tested. Its wager: nothing physical is an absolute number (a mass means nothing until a unit is chosen), only how one quantity stands to another. It fixes the dimensionless relations the world determines and concedes one scale, the anchor; a firewall shares a structure's form across domains, never a bare number. Its sharpest stakes: an axion-free zero of strong CP, few-GeV asymmetric dark matter, and the tau mass from Koide read forward. From the fundamental particles it carries this idea to the vacuum, the classical world, and physics' open problems. Book VII asks where the flavour geometry comes from. It fixes one concrete, frozen heterotic string vacuum — a Z_6-II orbifold of the E_8×E_8 mini-landscape, its provenance settled before any measured number is consulted — and asks whether the single amplitude the Koide relation leaves free descends from it. The programme holds throughout to one firewall: a structure's form may cross domains, a bare number never; and it keeps the line between what the mathematics closes and what stays open. No physical grade is raised; the Koide value stays open. Book VII is issued at one frozen epoch as three parts under a single manifest and version stamp — Part VII.1 (Corpus & Conditional Layers), Part VII.2 (the monograph edition) and Part VII.3 (the internal Annexes: the Ω-sections and the revision history). Part VII.3, The Source and the Cube: The Annexes, is the append-only provenance record behind Book VII — the hundreds of dated Ω-findings, the routes tried and refuted, the corrections booked with banners, and the full revision chronicle. It is not a publication of record and is never the sole terminal support of a claim typed closed: it is the working behind Parts VII.1 and VII.2, hash-frozen and available on request. Its discipline is the firewall in action. Every finding carries a typed Grade block with B_3=0 throughout — no physical grade raised anywhere — and superseded claims are retained with inline supersession banners rather than deleted. items.summary: Quantum resource theories usually begin with a prescribed free structure and ask what tasks become possible when a resource is supplied. We study the inverse problem of alchemical resource theories, which we define as resource theories admitting a resource that can both replicate itself exactly and universally program quantum instruments. Under natural consistency assumptions and branchwise complete freeness, we show that for qubit single systems only two nontrivial theories survive, up to a common local unitary change of basis: parity asymmetry and imaginarity. We further show that exact universality exhibits an all-or-nothing trade-off: any nonmaximal resource state can exactly program only free unitaries. These results demonstrate that prescribed operational capabilities can strongly constrain the underlying resource structure and reveal a fundamental trade-off between computational capability and the precision required for physical implementation.
items.title: Inverse Problem of Alchemical Resource Theory: Replication and Programming Single Out Imaginarity and Parity Asymmetry

items.summary: This monograph proposes a physical path from the proto-terrestrial system to the Earth–Moon system, in which a single event accounts for both the formation of the Moon and the delivery of terrestrial water. It does not claim to reconstruct a unique historical event. It asks instead whether a continuous, dynamically admissible, quantitatively constrained and falsifiable path can link a possible proto-terrestrial initial state to the system we observe. The proto-Earth considered here rotates close to its rotation limit, dilated by some thirteen per cent, its surface a magma ocean whose metallic iron and siderophile elements have already migrated to the core. It carries a secondary circumterrestrial reservoir, as forming planets do. A massive planetary body, denoted B, arrives from the cold outer regions and passes at three Earth radii, prograde and slightly inclined so as to clear the disk plane. During the few hours of close approach, the differential field of B lifts material from the intertropical belt of the magma ocean and strips metal-depleted silicate. That material joins the reservoir, circularises, and transport carries part of it beyond the Roche limit, where it accretes into a single dominant satellite. In the same encounter, B undergoes the reverse process: its volatile envelope, heated by the radiation of the magma ocean to some 2800 K, dilates until it overflows its own Roche lobe and yields its volatiles to the terrestrial system. The exchange is asymmetric, each body releasing what its physical state allows it to release. B then departs, carrying away part of the stripped terrestrial material together with the excess angular momentum, and leaving a trail whose re-accretion is spread over tens of millions of years. The central analytical result is that the specific angular momentum carried by each stripped layer admits a closed form in which the rotation term and the tidal impulse term share the same radial dependence. The condition for crossing the Roche limit therefore reduces to a single quantity combining the reduced rotation of the proto-Earth, its dilation, the mass of the perturber and its approach distance. Along the contour producing one lunar mass, this quantity remains constant to better than 0.5 per cent, so that the viable domain is a level surface rather than a volume: constraining one parameter fixes the others. Changing the internal structure of the proto-Earth alters the mass produced by a factor of nine but shifts the threshold by only six per cent, which confines the structural uncertainty to a single number. A prograde passage is required. The tidal impulse reverses sign in the retrograde case and closes the injection channel entirely. A test-particle calculation of the pre-existing reservoir confirms this independently: for a prograde passage, 18.5 per cent of the reservoir reaches the lunar window and 84 per cent of the mass remains bound in the circumterrestrial domain, whereas the retrograde control reduces the window fraction to 4.0 per cent and raises the escaping fraction to 42.5 per cent. Geochemistry follows from the same geometry rather than from additional hypotheses. Because the stripped material comes from the outer layers of a differentiated body, the iron deficit of the Moon, its isotopic identity with the terrestrial mantle in oxygen, titanium, chromium and tungsten, and the terrestrial signature of lunar water are consequences of provenance. The scientific status of the work is explicitly falsifiable. The viable domain is defined as the intersection of seventeen gates, and the monograph states for each whether it has been cleared on quantitative grounds, sketched, or still requires calculation. The path is viable only if a continuous domain of parameters satisfies the dynamical, geochemical, isotopic, thermodynamic and chronological constraints together, and it is excluded if no such domain exists.   https://github.com/Orion4622/moon-and-water

items.summary: Flow matching approaches to imaging inverse problems commonly incorporate measurements in two ways. Conditioning-based approaches supply measurement-derived information as a network input, often through concatenation, while inference-guided approaches combine an unconditional velocity field with a separate data-consistency update. In these common formulations, the forward model is not explicitly enforced within the learned conditional velocity field. We propose a principled parametrization of the measurement-conditional velocity field to solve inverse problems. Under linear interpolation, we express the conditional velocity $v(x_t,t,y)$ in terms of the posterior mean $E[x_1 | x_t,y]$, and characterize that mean as the unique minimizer of a variational objective whose data-consistency term is explicit. We further prove that the velocity field defines a probability flow from the source distribution to the measurement-conditioned posterior. Splitting the variational objective yields a conditional velocity parameterization with operator-dependent data-consistency updates, which we train end-to-end under the flow-matching objective, with no additional guidance at inference. Our method achieves state-of-the-art PSNR with $50\times$ fewer function evaluations than the strongest flow baseline. Varying the sampling steps provides test-time control over the distortion-perception trade-off without retraining.
items.title: Fast and Faithful: Principled Conditional Flow Matching for Inverse Problems

items.summary: Higher-order regularization has shown improved results over first-order methods such as total variation. In this paper, convergence of a piecewise linear finite element discretization is shown for the second-order total generalized variation functional. Additionally, this convergence result is extended to a spatiotemporal setting after the spatiotemporal function space is comprehensively introduced. In both cases, discrete minimizers converge to the continuous minimizer with rate $h^{1/4}$, matching the best known rate for finite element discretizations of total variation in the same general setting. Numerical experiments confirm the convergence rates and indicate faster convergence in practice. Comparisons with related spatial image reconstruction algorithms show comparable reconstruction results. The spatiotemporal case is discussed using the example of the inverse problem in electrocardiographic imaging, where the proposed functional improves the state of the art.
items.title: Total Generalized Variation for Inverse Problems Involving Piecewise Linear Finite Elements

items.summary: In this paper, we study an inverse boundary value problem for a generalized Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation with Westervelt-type nonlinearity and space-dependent coefficients. This third-order (in time) hyperbolic equation models nonlinear ultrasound propagation in viscous and thermally relaxing media. Assuming that the diffusivity and the sound speed are known a priori, we investigate the simultaneous stable determination of the friction coefficient, the weak damping coefficient, the potential, and the nonlinear coefficient from the associated Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. The proof combines the finite-difference linearization method with the construction of Gaussian beam and geometric optics solutions. These arguments reduce the inverse problem to stability estimates for (attenuated) geodesic ray transforms under the foliation condition. As a consequence, we obtain Hölder-type stability estimates of recovering the linear and nonlinear coefficients.
items.title: Stable determination of coefficients for the nonlinear third-order acoustic equations

items.summary: Large-scale multi-label text classification assigns a small subset of relevant labels to each document from a vocabulary containing thousands or tens of thousands of candidate labels. Although pretrained language models have improved semantic text representations, most representation-based approaches center their prediction pipelines on a primary encoder or combine auxiliary features within a single ranker. The complementarity between heterogeneous language models therefore remains insufficiently explored. We propose DualMLC, a dual-branch framework that processes the same document through an autoregressive decoder-only language model and a bidirectional encoder. Each branch maintains its own representation pathway and independently estimates relevance scores over the shared label space. DualMLC combines the two score vectors through late logit fusion, allowing shared evidence to reinforce relevant labels and branch-specific evidence to compensate for limitations in the other branch's representation. DualMLC achieves state-of-the-art results on three widely used large-scale multi-label text classification benchmarks. Ablation results further confirm that integrating the heterogeneous predictors produces stronger rankings than either branch alone. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/huiyegit/DualMLC.
items.title: LLM-Enhanced Dual-Branch Learning for Large-Scale Multi-Label Text Classification

items.summary: sEMG is vulnerable to various contaminants that distort signal morphology and spectral content. Accurate signal quality assessment (SQA) is essential for identifying such degradation and ensuring reliable clinical analyses and decisions. Recent neural network-based SQA methods achieve accurate quality estimation by learning complex contamination patterns, yet their black-box nature prevents clinicians from understanding or validating the reported scores and limits adaptability to application-specific quality definitions without retraining. To address these limitations, we propose Prism-SQA, an interpretable and adaptable neural framework that reformulates SQA as a physiology-aware source-separation and verification process. Prism-SQA decomposes each input signal into a clean sEMG component and five contaminant-specific components using a U-Net with bidirectional long short-term memory. Each separated contaminant component is examined by a Contaminant Fingerprint Verifier, which enforces physiological plausibility by comparing its temporal and spectral structure with canonical contaminant signatures. This design allows clinicians to inspect how each contaminant affects signal quality, grounding the assessment in transparent, signal-level evidence rather than opaque latent representations. Quality indices computed from the verified components further enable customization of quality criteria across clinical contexts without retraining. We evaluate Prism-SQA on continuous quality-score estimation using synthesized noisy sEMG from public Ninapro datasets and on binary quality classification using a clinical dysphagia dataset. Results show that Prism-SQA achieves competitive or better performance than contemporary black-box neural methods while providing explicit interpretability and adaptability, advancing toward practical and clinically aligned sEMG SQA.
items.title: Prism-SQA: An Interpretable and Adaptable Neural Framework for Surface Electromyography Quality Assessment

items.summary: Proposed framework: A) Large-scale brain dynamics regulate energy balance by coupling ongoing physiological inputs. B) Cognitive performance depends on the alignment between neural metastability and fluctuations in peripheral energy, a relationship conceptualized here as Body Energy Coupling. Within this framework, metabolism is not merely a constraining variable; rather, it reflects a regulated, coordinated interaction between oscillatory processes in the brain and body. Cognition can thus be understood as an emergent property—or rebound—of metabolic homeostasis. If so, energy-constrained oscillatory systems would represent a universal organizing substrate for energy equilibrium. In the specific case of living systems with known cognitive capabilities, cognition would be understood within this framework as an emergent property of this dynamic self-organizing system coupling. From this perspective, vulnerability arises from a disequilibrium between predictive (or active inference) processes and energy homeostasis mechanisms, leading to maladaptive system dynamics. This view is still preliminary and exploratory, as there is currently no empirical evidence supporting this theory; rather, it serves as a proof of concept. Diego Lombardo. The model uses coupled nonlinear oscillators defined on small-world networks to simulate large-scale neural activity, which is then bidirectionally coupled to a stochastic body signal and an evolving energy process. Within this framework, cognition is operationalized as a non-circular synthetic variable derived from the system’s ability to predict an independent external environment, allowing the separation of predictive neural dynamics, body–brain coupling, and energy regulation. items.summary: State-Dependent Ball-Screw Positioning Error Dataset: Operational Kinematic and ISO 230-2 Measurements Overview This dataset contains experimental positioning-error measurements acquired on a precision ball-screw-driven feed axis under systematically varied kinematic operating conditions. The dataset was generated using a dedicated automated test bench integrating servo-driven motion control, external laser interferometry with environmental compensation, distributed thermal monitoring, and automated data acquisition. The experimental campaign was designed to investigate positioning error beyond conventional static spatial characterization. In particular, the data enable positioning deviation to be analyzed as a state-dependent phenomenon influenced by the initial axis position, commanded displacement, preceding displacement, motion direction, reversal history, and motion velocity. Two complementary experimental datasets are provided: Operational kinematic measurements: acquired from independently sampled point-to-point movements over a broad range of kinematic states. Each experimental condition is defined as a batch and is repeated five times, with each repetition referred to as an action. ISO 230-2-based bidirectional positioning measurements: acquired under different spatial discretization and approach-velocity conditions, preserving the individual repeated measurements associated with each characterization curve. The operational dataset comprises two independent development campaigns containing a total of 2,000 distinct batches and an additional independent held-out evaluation campaign containing 300 batches . Since each batch was executed five times, the repository contains 10,000 action-level measurements for model development and 1,500 action-level measurements for independent evaluation. The ISO-based dataset contains 42 characterization curves resulting from seven spatial discretization values, three rotational velocities, and both motion directions. Individual experimental repetitions are preserved rather than providing only aggregated mean profiles. The repository therefore provides the experimental measurements required to reconstruct both the batch-level operational observations used for machine-learning modelling and the ISO-based spatial positioning-error profiles evaluated in the associated study. items.summary: Clinical timelines support treatment-window analysis and leakage-free modeling, but discharge summaries often obscure chronology and structured EHR tables describe only part of the patient course. We present a UID-preserving framework that links each narrative event occurrence to its source span and retains that identity through text-only estimation, structured-evidence retrieval, timestamped source-row grounding, and joint revision. We also present GAVEL, an LLM judge that compares two UID-aligned timelines against the narrative and structured record, to augment prior matching and temporal assessments. Across six open-weight models and 40 mixed-critical-care summaries, the GLM 5.2 multimodal revision, as compared to its text-only variant, improved temporal agreement without reducing event recovery and performed competitively with clinician annotations, while other model revisions showed smaller gains and lower overall performance. Ablations showed that UIDs primarily preserve event retention, whereas source-row linkage supports temporal placement. Blinded human review upheld most GAVEL findings, and controlled adjudication favored multimodal over text-only GLM 5.2 but did not for DeepSeek V3.2. In developing the UID and judge pipeline, we are able to demonstrate 43\% increased event recovery, a framework competitive with clinician annotations, and a system with occurrence-level provenance for both reconstruction and evaluation.
items.title: Anchoring Clinical Events in Time: UID-Preserving Multimodal Reconstruction and Source-Grounded Adjudication

items.summary: Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems, jointly interpreting images and natural language queries, hold significant promise across many domains, yet the privacy-sensitive nature of user data creates a fundamental barrier. Centralized training requires access to all data, while federated learning requires each client to host the full model. We propose USPLIT-VQA, a U-shaped split learning framework for privacy-preserving VQA in which each client retains the initial layers and the classification head while the server hosts the computationally heavy intermediate layers, keeping raw inputs and labels on the client device. We further introduce Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation (CAWA), a gradientsimilarity-based client scoring mechanism designed to reduce the influence of malicious updates. Experiments on four VQA datasets (VQA-RAD, SLAKE, PathVQA, and VizWiz) with two backbones show accuracy gains over Federated Learning for the Custom model and reduced accuracy for BiomedCLIP under the evaluated fixed split, alongside client memory reductions of up to 5.8X and communication reductions of up to 10.8X. With one malicious client, CAWA reduces the attacker's influence by over 98%, while experiments at higher corruption levels identify its limitations. Reconstruction experiments further show lower inversion quality under the evaluated attacks.
items.title: USPLIT-VQA: U-Shaped Split Learning for Visual Question Answering with Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation

items.summary: The archive includes analysis code for the HRS primary analysis, CHARLS independent replication, secondary hearing outcomes, additional diagnostic and sensitivity analyses, aggregate table and figure source data, and provenance documentation supporting the reported results. The archive includes analysis code for the HRS primary analysis, CHARLS independent replication, secondary hearing outcomes, selected sensitivity analyses, aggregate table and figure source data, and provenance documentation supporting the reported results. Participant-level HRS and CHARLS data are not included in this repository and are not redistributed by the authors. Eligible users must obtain the required source data independently from the respective HRS and CHARLS data portals and comply with the applicable data-use agreements. The HRS primary analysis uses the final strict source-confirmed incident-stroke definition; the earlier broader RAND-based definition is retained only as a historical exposure-definition sensitivity analysis. Some HRS analysis scripts are explicitly labelled RECONSTRUCTED_FOR_REPRODUCIBILITY because the original central execution drivers were not retained. These reconstructions were validated against frozen model objects, locked outputs, and numerical checks without changing the reported scientific results. This archive is intended for reproducibility from compatible locally constructed analytic objects rather than as a redistribution of cohort data or a one-command reconstruction from raw source files. Version 1.0 corresponds to the initial manuscript submission.
items.title: Reproducibility materials for "Incident stroke and subsequent self-rated hearing: replicated longitudinal evidence from the US HRS and Chinese CHARLS cohorts"

items.summary: Sanitized code and data reproducibility package for a manuscript currently under double-blind review at the Journal of Information Security and Applications. Author identity is withheld pending the outcome of review. items.summary: Parametric models of the human head are essential tools traditionally used in computer vision and graphics for animation, rendering, and reconstruction. More recently, they serve as crucial conditioning signals within generative large vision models, allowing for tight spatial control of generated imagery. However, existing publicly available models are typically limited in anatomical scope, modeling only outer geometry while ignoring intra-oral and ocular structures, and frequently suffer from reduced geometric quality stemming from low-fidelity input datasets. In this report we introduce a new parametric model dubbed Generative aNthropometric Model (GNM), named as a homophone of the human genome. GNM encompasses the head, face, neck, eyeballs, teeth, and tongue, and it is built on an extensive database of high-resolution 3D scans combined with high-quality anatomy specific artist-made samples. This report details the data provenance, the model architecture including the specialized sub-models for the ocular and intra-oral structures, and shows its SotA performance on fitting target 3D face scans. To foster community innovation, the complete GNM framework is made publicly available.
items.title: GNM Head: A Generative aNthropometric Model of the human head

items.summary: Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems, jointly interpreting images and natural language queries, hold significant promise across many domains, yet the privacy-sensitive nature of user data creates a fundamental barrier. Centralized training requires access to all data, while federated learning requires each client to host the full model. We propose USPLIT-VQA, a U-shaped split learning framework for privacy-preserving VQA in which each client retains the initial layers and the classification head while the server hosts the computationally heavy intermediate layers, keeping raw inputs and labels on the client device. We further introduce Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation (CAWA), a gradientsimilarity-based client scoring mechanism designed to reduce the influence of malicious updates. Experiments on four VQA datasets (VQA-RAD, SLAKE, PathVQA, and VizWiz) with two backbones show accuracy gains over Federated Learning for the Custom model and reduced accuracy for BiomedCLIP under the evaluated fixed split, alongside client memory reductions of up to 5.8X and communication reductions of up to 10.8X. With one malicious client, CAWA reduces the attacker's influence by over 98%, while experiments at higher corruption levels identify its limitations. Reconstruction experiments further show lower inversion quality under the evaluated attacks.
items.title: USPLIT-VQA: U-Shaped Split Learning for Visual Question Answering with Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation

items.summary: Flow matching approaches to imaging inverse problems commonly incorporate measurements in two ways. Conditioning-based approaches supply measurement-derived information as a network input, often through concatenation, while inference-guided approaches combine an unconditional velocity field with a separate data-consistency update. In these common formulations, the forward model is not explicitly enforced within the learned conditional velocity field. We propose a principled parametrization of the measurement-conditional velocity field to solve inverse problems. Under linear interpolation, we express the conditional velocity $v(x_t,t,y)$ in terms of the posterior mean $E[x_1 | x_t,y]$, and characterize that mean as the unique minimizer of a variational objective whose data-consistency term is explicit. We further prove that the velocity field defines a probability flow from the source distribution to the measurement-conditioned posterior. Splitting the variational objective yields a conditional velocity parameterization with operator-dependent data-consistency updates, which we train end-to-end under the flow-matching objective, with no additional guidance at inference. Our method achieves state-of-the-art PSNR with $50\times$ fewer function evaluations than the strongest flow baseline. Varying the sampling steps provides test-time control over the distortion-perception trade-off without retraining.
items.title: Fast and Faithful: Principled Conditional Flow Matching for Inverse Problems

items.summary: In this paper, we study an inverse boundary value problem for a generalized Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation with Westervelt-type nonlinearity and space-dependent coefficients. This third-order (in time) hyperbolic equation models nonlinear ultrasound propagation in viscous and thermally relaxing media. Assuming that the diffusivity and the sound speed are known a priori, we investigate the simultaneous stable determination of the friction coefficient, the weak damping coefficient, the potential, and the nonlinear coefficient from the associated Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. The proof combines the finite-difference linearization method with the construction of Gaussian beam and geometric optics solutions. These arguments reduce the inverse problem to stability estimates for (attenuated) geodesic ray transforms under the foliation condition. As a consequence, we obtain Hölder-type stability estimates of recovering the linear and nonlinear coefficients.
items.title: Stable determination of coefficients for the nonlinear third-order acoustic equations

items.summary: BanglaVLP-5K is a curated high-resolution image dataset of Bangladeshi vehicles and real-world traffic scenes, including images in which vehicle licence plates are visible. The dataset was developed to provide a reusable collection of real-world vehicle imagery from the Bangladeshi traffic environment for computer vision, intelligent transportation, image-analysis, and related research. The original image collection contained 4,993 images. All source images underwent a systematic technical and curation workflow including image-readability verification, file-integrity assessment, SHA-256 hashing, exact-duplicate analysis, perceptual near-duplicate and same-scene candidate identification, repeated-source-basename review, and conservative visual curation. Following the final curation stage, 4,955 images were retained for the public dataset, while 38 visually redundant near-identical images were excluded. The final dataset contains 4,955 technically readable images with 4,955 unique SHA-256 checksums. The median image resolution is approximately 2448 × 3264 pixels, corresponding to approximately 7.99 megapixels. The final image collection occupies approximately 14.52 GB. The dataset is distributed across five size-balanced image archives. Each archive contains an “images” directory holding the curated images and a “part_manifest.csv” file that provides the image identifiers, publication filenames, original filenames, file sizes, SHA-256 checksums, and archive-part information for the images contained in that archive. A separate metadata and documentation archive is also provided. It contains the complete final image manifest, image-level SHA-256 checksums, the dataset data dictionary, the Zenodo archive-part assignment, dataset summary statistics, final integrity-check results, the curation protocol, quality-control documentation, a dataset card, a repository file guide, and figures describing the dataset-preparation workflow and image-resolution distribution. Users should consult the included README, dataset card, data dictionary, curation protocol, quality-control documentation, final image manifest, and SHA-256 checksum file before using the dataset.

items.summary: This record contains the cumulative Lean-verified Chronos dimensionality and Möbius-field formalization from M1 through M6. The work formally separates a scalar temporal point-state from the dimensionality of the ambient coordinate space and from the scalar field defined over that space. In the verified construction, the Chronos x-value remains a scalar state, while spatial dimensionality is carried independently by explicitly typed Euclidean coordinate spaces. The M1–M6 chain begins with the Möbius sign-reversal structure, including one-lap orientation reversal, two-lap state recovery, and the continuous zero-crossing result. It then introduces the exact dimensional field architecture, allowing the same scalar point-state to be represented in one-dimensional, three-dimensional, and generic finite-dimensional fields without identifying the scalar value itself with a dimension. The later milestones prove exact transfer of the one-dimensional temporal profile into arbitrary-dimensional scalar fields, radial specialization of that construction, and the resulting dimension-dependent geometry of constant-state level sets. In three spatial dimensions, the exact Chronos x-state is formally identified with a spherical level shell inside the previously verified radial gravity field. The series further proves the exact field gradient and gradient-coupled acceleration on the x-shell, preserves the established Newtonian correspondence under the stated gravity calibration, and extends the construction to moving x-level shells and time-indexed radial fields. The final milestone establishes a generic dynamic radial-gradient theorem for arbitrary differentiable evolving radial profiles. The result shows formally how a local radial field slope determines the corresponding spatial gradient and gradient-coupled acceleration, including exact zero-response and opposite-slope response theorems. The complete M1–M6 dependency chain kernel-checked successfully against the pinned OpenAI NavierStokesAndEuler environment. The cumulative build completed 9,327 Lake jobs. Thirty-seven explicit axiom checks were performed. The audited declarations depend only on standard Lean/Mathlib foundational principles and contain no project-specific axioms, sorry , admit , or sorryAx proof placeholders. This formalization proves the dimensional field architecture and its stated consequences. It establishes that scalar temporal state and ambient coordinate dimension are mathematically distinct objects and proves how one scalar state lifts into dimension-dependent field geometry. A later formal target is to derive or select dimensional structure dynamically rather than supplying the coordinate dimension as an index. The archive includes Lean source, reproducibility scripts, verification logs, axiom audits, deterministic numerical checks, provenance information, checksums, and milestone documentation.

items.summary: This dataset and replication package accompanies a comparative spatial-network analysis of the structural resilience of international digital connectivity across the 32 NATO member states and Russia. The study integrates active international submarine communication cable (SCC) systems with operational cross-border terrestrial fibre connectivity (LCC) and evaluates how much direct external-partner connectivity remains under progressively more severe disruption scenarios. The principal outcome is Partner Retention, defined as the share of baseline direct external partners that remain connected after a disruption. The analysis includes random SCC failures, geographically correlated disruption, complete SCC outage, terrestrial partner concentration tests, alternative clustering thresholds, and additional robustness checks. Under a complete submarine-cable outage, Russia retains 92.3% of its direct external partners, compared with a median of 33.3% among NATO members with active submarine-cable connectivity. The results indicate that this structural advantage is primarily associated with Russia’s extensive cross-border terrestrial fibre network rather than a larger submarine-cable system. The package includes R scripts, processed replication data, selected raw submarine-cable inputs, result tables, figures, QGIS outputs, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, metadata, and methodological notes. The dataset measures structural connectivity rather than traffic volume, bandwidth, latency, economic loss, repair time, or dynamic rerouting capacity.

items.summary: Production artificial intelligence systems are increasingly assessed not only by whether they generate accurate predictions, but by whether the operating organization can reconstruct, explain, and defend the exact evidence behind an individual outcome after the surrounding system has changed. This paper develops a quantitative framework for measuring that property, which we term evidence continuity. The framework is grounded primarily and foundationally in the work of Mesbaul Haque Sazu, specifically his Governed Decision-Intelligence (GDI) reference architecture [22] and his Full-Stack Production-Platform Reference Architecture [21]. GDI establishes the decision as the unit of assurance and makes evidence binding, lineage, validation, calibrated confidence, deterministic explanation, human oversight, and outcome closure explicit control obligations. The Full-Stack architecture extends these obligations into runtime operation through capture-at-commit, execution records, trajectory-level observability, before-commit gating, and closed-loop production control. Building directly on and leveraging these two foundations, this paper contributes a measurement layer that sits above them. We model an AI system as a typed, versioned, directed evidence graph and introduce three constructs: the Evidence Continuity Graph (ECG), the Trace Completeness Ratio (TCR), and the Governance Coverage Index (GCI). We formalize per-decision and aggregate estimators, extend the naive independence model to a correlated-failure regime using a Beta-Binomial mixture, and derive path-based reconstructability over admissible evidence paths. A synthetic benchmark of 2,800 investigation traces demonstrates how time-to-trace, incomplete-trace probability, and reconstruction probability respond as evidence coverage varies. The results are illustrative rather than empirical claims about deployed systems. The paper concludes with a reference implementation architecture, threshold-setting guidance calibrated to deployment risk, a security and failure analysis, and a research agenda for validating evidence continuity on real production workloads.

items.summary: The Earth That Heard   The Earth That Heard is not presented as a literary reconstruction built around biblical verses. It records a textual architecture that the author argues is already present in the Torah itself — a structure that emerged through fifteen years of research into Biblical Hebrew morphology, roots, recurring letter patterns, and the internal organization of the text. The essay traces a continuous thread from the murder of Abel in Genesis to Joshua's altar on Mount Ebal. Motifs that initially appear independent — earth and blood, firstfruit and firstborn, field and El Shaddai, rising and place, sacrifice, Shechem, the opening of the earth, and the return of the firstfruits — progressively converge into a single narrative structure. The central proposal is that Abel's unfinished offering, Cain's failure, and the wounded earth are not abandoned episodes: their resolution unfolds across the Torah and reaches completion in Joshua. items.summary: The book series The Stream and the Algebra presents a speculative research programme — a thought-experiment in the mathematics of relation, offered for scrutiny, not yet peer-reviewed or tested. Its wager: nothing physical is an absolute number (a mass means nothing until a unit is chosen), only how one quantity stands to another. It fixes the dimensionless relations the world determines and concedes one scale, the anchor; a firewall shares a structure's form across domains, never a bare number. Its sharpest stakes: an axion-free zero of strong CP, few-GeV asymmetric dark matter, and the tau mass from Koide read forward. From the fundamental particles it carries this idea to the vacuum, the classical world, and physics' open problems. Book VII asks where the flavour geometry comes from. It fixes one concrete, frozen heterotic string vacuum — a Z_6-II orbifold of the E_8×E_8 mini-landscape, its provenance settled before any measured number is consulted — and asks whether the single amplitude the Koide relation leaves free descends from it. The programme holds throughout to one firewall: a structure's form may cross domains, a bare number never; and it keeps the line between what the mathematics closes and what stays open. No physical grade is raised; the Koide value stays open. Book VII is issued at one frozen epoch as three parts under a single manifest and version stamp — Part VII.1 (Corpus & Conditional Layers), Part VII.2 (the monograph edition) and Part VII.3 (the internal Annexes: the Ω-sections and the revision history). Part VII.3, The Source and the Cube: The Annexes, is the append-only provenance record behind Book VII — the hundreds of dated Ω-findings, the routes tried and refuted, the corrections booked with banners, and the full revision chronicle. It is not a publication of record and is never the sole terminal support of a claim typed closed: it is the working behind Parts VII.1 and VII.2, hash-frozen and available on request. Its discipline is the firewall in action. Every finding carries a typed Grade block with B_3=0 throughout — no physical grade raised anywhere — and superseded claims are retained with inline supersession banners rather than deleted. items.summary: This dataset and replication package accompanies a comparative spatial-network analysis of the structural resilience of international digital connectivity across the 32 NATO member states and Russia. The study integrates active international submarine communication cable (SCC) systems with operational cross-border terrestrial fibre connectivity (LCC) and evaluates how much direct external-partner connectivity remains under progressively more severe disruption scenarios. The principal outcome is Partner Retention, defined as the share of baseline direct external partners that remain connected after a disruption. The analysis includes random SCC failures, geographically correlated disruption, complete SCC outage, terrestrial partner concentration tests, alternative clustering thresholds, and additional robustness checks. Under a complete submarine-cable outage, Russia retains 92.3% of its direct external partners, compared with a median of 33.3% among NATO members with active submarine-cable connectivity. The results indicate that this structural advantage is primarily associated with Russia’s extensive cross-border terrestrial fibre network rather than a larger submarine-cable system. The package includes R scripts, processed replication data, selected raw submarine-cable inputs, result tables, figures, QGIS outputs, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, metadata, and methodological notes. The dataset measures structural connectivity rather than traffic volume, bandwidth, latency, economic loss, repair time, or dynamic rerouting capacity.
items.title: Structural Resilience of International Digital Connectivity under Submarine Cable Disruption: NATO Members and Russia

items.summary: This replication package contains the data, R scripts, figures, and documentation used in the study “Turkey–Greece Naval Procurement Rivalry, 1990–2025.” The study examines the temporal structure of naval procurement competition between Turkey and Greece using annual data for 1990–2025. The main empirical series are derived from the SIPRI Arms Transfers Database and SIPRI Transfer Register. Annual Ships Trend Indicator Value (TIV) data are used to measure international naval platform deliveries, while order-year information is used to distinguish procurement decisions from subsequent deliveries. World Bank World Development Indicators are used for the macroeconomic control variable. The analysis tests contemporaneous and 1–3-year lagged relationships between Greek and Turkish naval procurement. Robustness checks include Newey–West HAC standard errors, alternative bandwidths, leave-one-out tests, influential-year exclusions, winsorization, placebo leads, and multiple-testing corrections using the Benjamini–Hochberg, Holm, and Bonferroni procedures. All data preparation and statistical analyses were conducted in R. The results show that Turkish and Greek naval procurement processes are temporally connected rather than independent. The strongest delivery-to-delivery association appears at a two-year lag. Greek naval deliveries are also associated with Turkish international naval orders one year later, while reverse-direction models identify associations between Turkish deliveries and subsequent Greek international orders. The overall pattern is consistent with reciprocal and temporally clustered modernization cycles rather than a fixed one-way action–reaction process. The repository includes cleaned analytical datasets, R scripts, figures, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, citation metadata, and the manuscript. Raw proprietary or redistribution-restricted source files are not included; users should consult the original SIPRI and World Bank sources where applicable. Version 1.2 adds the reviewer-requested stationarity diagnostics, first-difference sensitivity analyses, and leave-one-programme-window-out tests. The revised package also includes updated regression outputs and the reviewer-revised manuscript. The main research design and core delivery-to-delivery finding remain unchanged.
items.title: Turkey–Greece Naval Procurement Rivalry, 1990–2025: Replication Data and Code

items.summary: BanglaVLP-5K is a curated high-resolution image dataset of Bangladeshi vehicles and real-world traffic scenes, including images in which vehicle licence plates are visible. The dataset was developed to provide a reusable collection of real-world vehicle imagery from the Bangladeshi traffic environment for computer vision, intelligent transportation, image-analysis, and related research. The original image collection contained 4,993 images. All source images underwent a systematic technical and curation workflow including image-readability verification, file-integrity assessment, SHA-256 hashing, exact-duplicate analysis, perceptual near-duplicate and same-scene candidate identification, repeated-source-basename review, and conservative visual curation. Following the final curation stage, 4,955 images were retained for the public dataset, while 38 visually redundant near-identical images were excluded. The final dataset contains 4,955 technically readable images with 4,955 unique SHA-256 checksums. The median image resolution is approximately 2448 × 3264 pixels, corresponding to approximately 7.99 megapixels. The final image collection occupies approximately 14.52 GB. The dataset is distributed across five size-balanced image archives. Each archive contains an “images” directory holding the curated images and a “part_manifest.csv” file that provides the image identifiers, publication filenames, original filenames, file sizes, SHA-256 checksums, and archive-part information for the images contained in that archive. A separate metadata and documentation archive is also provided. It contains the complete final image manifest, image-level SHA-256 checksums, the dataset data dictionary, the Zenodo archive-part assignment, dataset summary statistics, final integrity-check results, the curation protocol, quality-control documentation, a dataset card, a repository file guide, and figures describing the dataset-preparation workflow and image-resolution distribution. Images in the public archives use standardized identifiers and filenames such as BDVLP_000001.jpg. Original source filenames are preserved in the metadata manifest for provenance and reproducibility. The image packaging procedure preserves the original source image bytes and does not resize or re-encode the images. BanglaVLP-5K is released as an annotation-free curated raw-image dataset. It does not include manually verified licence-plate bounding boxes, licence-plate character transcriptions, or manually verified vehicle-category ground-truth labels. Any automatically generated vehicle-category estimates present in the metadata are provided only as auxiliary technical descriptors and must not be interpreted as verified annotations or ground-truth labels. The dataset may be useful for computer vision research, vehicle and traffic-scene analysis, domain adaptation, transfer learning, image-quality and robustness studies, development and evaluation of image-processing methods, and the creation of future manually annotated derivative datasets for vehicle or licence-plate-related research. Users should consult the included README, dataset card, data dictionary, curation protocol, quality-control documentation, final image manifest, and SHA-256 checksum file before using the dataset.
items.title: BanglaVLP-5K: A Curated High-Resolution Image Dataset of Bangladeshi Vehicles and Licence Plates in Real-World Traffic Environments

items.summary: This record contains the reproducibility package accompanying the manuscript “A Projected Semiexplicit Integrator for Dissipative Systems with Configuration-Dependent Kinetic Energy: Contact-Herglotz Formulation and Benchmarks.” The package provides the Julia implementation, pinned computational environment, benchmark parameters, analysis and plotting scripts, automated tests, CSV result files, generated figures and LaTeX table bodies, and per-run metadata supporting the results reported in the manuscript and its Supplementary Material. The implementation covers the projected semiexplicit contact-Herglotz integrator and the numerical benchmarks used to assess convergence, contact and conformal structure preservation, projection activity and load, long-time behavior, work-precision performance, variable friction, Tao extended-phase-space baselines, Kevrekidis-type contact splittings, and the lifted implicit midpoint comparison. A single documented driver, analysis/run_all.jl , regenerates the numerical results, tables, and figures used by the study. The archived environment requires Julia 1.12 or later, and the reported results were generated with Julia 1.12.6. The source code is distributed under the MIT License. Generated results and documentation are distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0). Associated preprint: arXiv:2608.17198.
items.title: Reproducibility package for "A Projected Semiexplicit Integrator for Dissipative Systems with Configuration-Dependent Kinetic Energy: Contact-Herglotz Formulation and Benchmarks"

items.summary: Sanitized code and data reproducibility package for a manuscript currently under double-blind review at the Journal of Information Security and Applications. Author identity is withheld pending the outcome of review. The package contains two independently generated archives: (1) model-I-single-branch/ — a single clock-controlled ternary LFSR generator over GF(3) (controller LFSR A + data LFSR B), together with its exact period and design-condition checkers, a statistical analysis suite, a 14-family ternary long-sequence test battery, and a cryptanalytic attack suite (basic correlation, embedding, fast correlation, Berlekamp-Massey reconstruction, and a linear-consistency/clock-control attack). Includes all 40 archived experiment runs across 8 controller/data degree configurations. (2) model-II-three-branch/ — a three-branch clock-controlled generator over GF(3) combined through a quadratic nonlinear ternary function, together with period/design analysis, algebraic/spectral characterization of the combiner, an aggregate statistical pipeline, avalanche diffusion experiments, a matched attack suite, and an exact key-stream-reuse detector. A full SHA-256 manifest (MANIFEST_SHA256.tsv) and verification script (verify_checksums.py) are included to allow integrity checking of every file. See README.md for directory structure, provenance notes, a documented anonymity sanitization log, and instructions to reproduce all reported results. See CORRESPONDENCE.md for a mapping between source files and the tables/figures of the manuscript. Source code (*.py, *.bat) is released under the MIT License. Generated data, results, logs, CSV aggregates, and figures are released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
items.title: Reproducibility package for "Clock-Controlled Ternary Sequence Generators over GF(3): Exact Periods, Statistical Structure, and Cryptanalytic Comparison of Single-Branch and Three-Branch Nonlinear Architectures"

items.summary: Reproducibility package supporting an analysis of sustainability transition in Sarawak, Malaysia. The repository contains curated analytical and processed datasets, acquisition and processing notebooks, model outputs, robustness analyses, figures, quality-assurance records, provenance documentation and detailed reproduction guidance. The research examines whether low-carbon development constitutes a sustainability transition when ecological integrity, biodiversity and climate-conditioned environmental vulnerability are considered alongside energy and development outcomes. The package contains 103 scientific files together with repository control documentation. Eleven public-facing scientific files were prepared as portability-safe or publication-safe copies without changing the underlying scientific results. Three RQ5 outputs carry explicit provenance warnings because their original computational specification could not be fully reconstructed; these limitations are transparently documented. Third-party and derived datasets remain governed by their original licensing and attribution terms.
